skill.displayName: 别瞎说 - AI事实核查器/Checktruth - AI Fact-Checker

llm.summary: The core fact-checking skill is coherent, but bundled optional scripts can send user content and API keys to external or custom LLM endpoints, so users should review them before use.

dimensions.detail: Optional reference scripts read API keys from environment variables and transmit questions, answers, facts, and generated prompts to third-party LLM providers; OpenAI-compatible scripts also accept unrestricted API base URLs without validation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Core use has no install step, but the optional reference implementation instructs pip install from unpinned requirements, creating supply-chain and reproducibility risk for users who run it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions stay focused on fact checking and source-backed scoring; they force Chinese output, which is a usability/locale limitation rather than evidence of malicious behavior.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No background service, privilege escalation, startup hook, or cross-session agent persistence was found; the optional multi_model_verify.py script writes verification_result.json containing submitted content and model responses.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The declared purpose is fact checking via WebSearch/WebFetch and built-in LLM reasoning, which matches the main SKILL.md instructions; the reference folder adds optional real multi-model verification using external APIs.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Core installation appears suitable for fact-checking workflows, but do not run the optional reference scripts on confidential text unless you accept sending that text to the configured LLM providers. If using the reference code, use a dedicated virtual environment, pin dependencies, set least-privileged API keys, avoid exposing unrelated environment variables, and do not set custom API base URLs unless you fully trust the endpoint.
llm.findings:
[TT3] expected: Using API keys in authenticated LLM requests is expected for the optional reference implementation, but unrestricted OPENAI_API_BASE/LLM_API_BASE handling is a real hardening gap because credentials could be sent to an unintended endpoint if the environment is manipulated.
[E1] expected: External transmission to LLM providers is disclosed as optional reference behavior and is aligned with real multi-model verification, but users must treat submitted content as leaving their local environment.
[SQP-2] expected: The package discloses that optional reference code may send user text to third-party LLM providers; the scripts themselves do not add an interactive consent or redaction step before sending.
[T09] unexpected: The static finding about unrestricted configurable endpoints is supported by the reference code and is not necessary for ordinary core skill operation; it affects users who run the optional OpenAI-compatible scripts.
[T08] unexpected: The optional requirements.txt uses open-ended dependency ranges; no malicious dependency evidence was found, but installations are not reproducible.
[P6] unexpected: The cited code loads local prompt templates for its own LLM calls; I did not find evidence that it extracts or leaks the agent's system or developer prompts.
[AE1] unexpected: The scanner reported partial SKILL.md inspection, but this review inspected the complete 482-line SKILL.md file.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-only prompts and output are plainly present and aligned with the skill's Chinese-facing examples, but they limit user language choice rather than indicating malicious behavior.
